dances-with-wolves-1990.gazette: Much of the dialogue is spoken in Lakota, with the production leaning on language coaching, period costuming, and reconstructed camp life shot out on the South Dakota plains. Lakota speakers have since flagged what the reconstruction missed, most often the language's gendered speech forms, delivered by male characters in the feminine. The authenticity claim and its audit have traveled together ever since.

the-age-of-innocence-1993.gazette: Scorsese's 1870s New York was assembled from period sources: etiquette manuals, menus, calling-card protocol, table settings researched down to the placement of the glassware. Troy, New York, stood in for much of old Manhattan, its untouched blocks doubling for a city that had built over itself. The result reads less as decor than as evidence.

l-a-confidential-1997.gazette: The film rebuilds Los Angeles circa 1953 — the Formosa Cafe, the police machinery, the tabloid trade — and drops a fictional scandal sheet where Confidential magazine actually stood. Confidential was the real article: a national monthly that bought tips from insiders and studio staff, and it collapsed only after California took it to court. The city in the frame came with a press corps built to sell it out.
l-a-confidential-1997.prism: The period detail cuts against the nostalgia it invites — the sunshine and the smear operation are the same 1953. Getting the tabloid right means the corruption isn't a plot device, it's part of the set.

flowers-of-shanghai-1998.gazette: Every scene takes place indoors, in the flower houses of 1880s Shanghai: oil-lamp light, opium trays, the slow protocol of drinking games and negotiated contracts. Hou built the interiors on a soundstage and never cut away to a street, so the reconstruction is total and airless by design. The custom is not background here; it is the entire mechanism of the plot.

chunhyang-2000.gazette: Im Kwon-taek frames the Chunhyang story inside a live pansori performance, letting one singer's narration and a single drum set the film's pace. The Joseon world onscreen — costume, rank, the etiquette of the magistrate's court and its punishments — is staged to match what the song describes. The film goes where the voice goes.

in-the-mood-for-love-2000.gazette: Wong's 1962 Hong Kong — the Shanghainese boarding houses, the crowded corridors, the cheongsam worn to fetch noodles — was largely reconstructed in Bangkok, because the Hong Kong of that year no longer existed to shoot. Thai streets and interiors were dressed to stand in for a neighborhood long since redeveloped. What reaches the screen is a period city assembled at a distance from itself.
in-the-mood-for-love-2000.prism: A film about people who can't return to what they had also had to be built somewhere else. The exactness of the reconstruction is a measure of how completely the original was cleared away.

joint-security-area-2000.gazette: Filming inside the real Joint Security Area at Panmunjom was never an option, so the production built a full-scale replica outside Seoul: the blue conference huts, the demarcation line, the guard posts facing each other across it. The set is accurate enough that the geometry of the standoff — a few meters of concrete between two armies — does most of the film's work. What could not be entered was rebuilt to measure.

no-2012.gazette: The 1988 plebiscite is reconstructed down to its campaign hardware: the rainbow logo, the jingle, the nightly quarter-hour of television each side was allotted. Larraín shot on the same period ¾-inch video the archive was recorded on, so the invented footage and the genuine footage sit in one grain. Chile voted a dictatorship out on an advertising campaign.

court-2015.gazette: Tamhane's sessions court runs on the real thing: adjournments, dress codes, a colonial-era statute read aloud, clerks moving paper at their own speed. Hearings play out in long static takes with much of the cast drawn from nonprofessionals, and the case against a folk singer advances by postponement rather than verdict. The procedure is filmed at the length procedure actually takes.
court-2015.prism: When the accuracy is that patient, the punishment stops being the sentence and becomes the calendar. Nobody in the room has to intend cruelty for the machine to deliver it.

in-this-corner-of-the-world-2016.gazette: The animation is drawn from archival research into wartime Kure and Hiroshima: rationing rules, street layouts since erased, the warships in the harbor, air-raid warnings timed to the logs that recorded them. Domestic work — stretching rice, mending, cooking with less each month — is rendered with the same care as the bombing. The record it draws on is a household record.

phantom-thread-2017.gazette: The House of Woodcock was built as a working couture house, with a costume team cutting, fitting, and finishing garments on camera in 1950s technique. Day-Lewis learned dressmaking for the role, reconstructing a period gown from the inside out before shooting began. Most of what the film shows of the trade is the unglamorous part: pins, hems, and the hours before a fitting.

the-souvenir-2019.gazette: Hogg withheld a conventional script, handing her cast scene outlines and letting the dialogue be found on the day. The Knightsbridge flat where she lived in the 1980s was rebuilt full-scale as a set, and the film was shot inside a reconstruction of her own address. The autobiography is literal down to the floor plan.
the-souvenir-2019.prism: Rebuilding the flat is one kind of accuracy; keeping the lead actor from knowing what happens next is another. The method puts her exactly where the character stands — informed late, by events.

flee-2021.gazette: Amin's account was recorded over years of conversation with a friend who became his director, then animated rather than filmed, because telling it under his own face was not safe. The route it traces — Kabul, Moscow, the smugglers' network, Copenhagen — is his own biography. The drawing is what makes the testimony sayable.

licorice-pizza-2021.gazette: The 1973 San Fernando Valley is reassembled address by address: Tail o' the Cock, Fat Bernie's, Jerry Frick's waterbed showroom, all of it shot on film stock chosen to match. The fuel shortage that strands the Valley mid-picture was the real one, and the businesses onscreen were real businesses, most of them long gone. The period here is the location scout's work as much as the writer's.

fire-of-love-2022.gazette: Almost every image in the film was shot by Katia and Maurice Krafft themselves, across two decades of getting nearer to erupting volcanoes than anyone else was willing to go. The archive they left is vast, and it ends where they did, at Mount Unzen in 1991. The record and the subject are the same footage.
fire-of-love-2022.prism: They filmed to make the danger legible to other people, and that same habit kept them standing where the footage had to be shot. The archive is both the argument for the risk and the receipt for it.
